summary: notification-service is being OOMKilled ~every 22h by a steady heap leak, not by a Kafka replay. Deploy dep-5402 (v3.8.0, 2026-03-21T00:00, 'Add in-memory template cache for email rendering') added a ConcurrentHashMap TemplateCache keyed by template+locale+userSegment with no eviction bound. Immediately after the deploy, memory_pct switched from flat ~48% (stable for days) to a monotonic linear climb, producing OOMKilled restarts at 03-21T22:59, 03-22T21:59 and 03-23T19:59; the cache itself logs 'size=188100 entries, evictions=0' (then reset to 9000 after restart). The reported Kafka-replay theory is contradicted: the retention config change (cfg-2410) happened 2026-03-23T18:00, ~21h after the climb began and after two prior OOMs; consumer_lag is normal (~50-90) until the restart instant, so lag/delayed emails are a downstream symptom of the restart. CPU (~25%) and request_rate (~140 req/s) are flat, ruling out load/capacity. Root cause: bad_deployment in notification-service.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Unbounded in-memory TemplateCache leak introduced by deploy v3.8.0 causes OOMKill
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Deploy dep-5402 (v3.8.0) added a TemplateCache (ConcurrentHashMap keyed by template+locale+userSegment) with no eviction bound. The cache grows monotonically (~100 entries/min), steadily consuming heap until the container hits its memory limit and is OOMKilled roughly every 22h; the resulting restart causes the ~25 min email delay and transient consumer-lag/5xx spikes. Fault originates in notification-service code.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5402 deployed at 2026-03-21T00:00 adds unbounded TemplateCache
memory_pct inflects from flat ~48% to steady linear climb at 03-21T01:20
cache reported growing with evictions=0 (188100 -> reset to 9000 after restart)
restart causes consumer-lag and 5xx spikes and delayed emails

assumptions: Heap is dominated by the new cache (no direct heap-dump/heap-by-object telemetry available)
The memory limit was unchanged (no config change for notification-service in window)

ranked_hypotheses.title: Kafka replay/retention change after maintenance overloads consumer
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The reported theory: Kafka maintenance + reduced retention (cfg-2410) triggers a replay that the consumer chokes on, causing OOM. Fault would originate in/depend on Kafka.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The cfg-2410 retention change landed 2026-03-23T18:00, ~21h after the memory climb began (03-21T01:20) and after two earlier OOMs (03-21T22:59, 03-22T21:59). consumer_lag stays normal (~50-90) until the OOM moment itself, then spikes — lag is a consequence of the restart, not the trigger. kafka CPU flat ~35%, no kafka errors.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Load/capacity growth or resource exhaustion without a triggering change
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Traffic grew beyond provisioned capacity, or the container simply ran out of memory/resource with no faulty change.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: request_rate (~140 req/s) and CPU (~25%) are flat across the whole window; capacity did not change. Memory growth is a deterministic ~22h sawtooth starting exactly at the deploy, which points to a code leak (bad_deployment) rather than load outgrowing capacity.

facts.statement: notification-service v3.8.0 added a ConcurrentHashMap TemplateCache keyed by template+locale+userSegment, deployed 2026-03-21T00:00, not rolled back.
Memory was flat ~48% for days then began a steady linear climb beginning ~2026-03-21T01:20, right after the v3.8.0 deploy.
Memory follows a ~22h sawtooth with OOMKilled restarts at 03-21T22:59, 03-22T21:59, 03-23T19:59 (restarts counter 1/2/3).
TemplateCache logs unbounded size with evictions=0 (188100 entries pre-OOM; reset to 9000 post-restart).
CPU (~25%) and request_rate (~140 req/s) are flat throughout, so load/capacity did not change.
consumer_lag is normal (~50-90) and spikes only during the OOM/restart windows, indicating lag is a consequence of the restart.
The Kafka retention config change (cfg-2410) occurred at 2026-03-23T18:00, ~21h after the leak began and after two earlier OOMs.
kafka shows flat CPU ~35% and no incident-related errors.
5xx error_rate spikes (max ~13-14%) occur only in restart buckets; baseline ~0.2%.
Historical incidents link consumer-lag spikes to Kafka broker maintenance/reassignment.

assumptions: The new TemplateCache dominates heap growth; no object-level heap dump telemetry is available to prove allocation source.
container memory limit is unchanged (no notification-service config change observed in window).
The cache is keyed by template+locale+userSegment whose cardinality is effectively unbounded, so entries accumulate without hits.

timeline.event: Deploy dep-5402 v3.8.0 'Add in-memory template cache' goes live
Memory begins steady linear climb (leak onset)
Third OOMKilled restart (restarts=3); consumer lag spike window follows

recommended_actions.action: Roll back / revert dep-5402 (v3.8.0) or hotfix the TemplateCache to add a bounded eviction policy (size/size+TTL) and disable the cache path.
recommended_actions.rationale: The leak starts exactly when this deploy goes live and the cache is proven unbounded with evictions=0; removing it stops the ~22h OOM cycle.

recommended_actions.action: Temporarily raise the container memory limit / increase restart guard to buy time and reduce customer-visible email delays until the fix ships.
recommended_actions.rationale: Mitigates OOM-driven restarts and the resulting ~25 min email delay and 5xx spikes.

recommended_actions.action: Add heap/object histograms and cache-size metrics with eviction counts so unbounded growth is detectable before OOM.
recommended_actions.rationale: Current telemetry needed a manual log read of 'evictions=0' to confirm the leak; proactive metrics would catch recurrence.

recommended_actions.action: Review TemplateCache key cardinality (template+locale+userSegment) and cap per-segment entries; add a load test asserting bounded heap over a 24h soak.
recommended_actions.rationale: Unbounded key space is the underlying design flaw that let the leak grow for 22h undetected.

data_gaps: No heap-dump/object-allocation telemetry to positively attribute heap growth to TemplateCache entries.
kafka service exposes no consumer_lag metric (only cpu_pct, messages_in_per_s, under_replicated_partitions), so the Kafka-side replay volume during 03-23T18:00-20:00 could not be directly measured.
No notification-service config change logs exist for the window, so container memory-limit changes cannot be confirmed (assumed unchanged).
email-provider has no telemetry, so external delay contribution cannot be measured (though not the observed failure mode).

findings.statement: notification-service deployed v3.8.0 'Add in-memory template cache for email rendering' using 'TemplateCache (ConcurrentHashMap) keyed by template+locale+userSegment' on 2026-03-21T00:00:00Z by s.menon; status live, not rolled back.

notification-service memory_pct was flat ~47-49% from 2026-03-18 through 2026-03-21T00:00 (e.g. 48.14 avg), then inflected to a steady linear climb starting ~2026-03-21T01:20 (50.75 -> 54.24 -> 57.82 -> 61.21 -> 68.47 -> 71.42).

memory_pct shows a repeating ~22h sawtooth: climbs from ~47% to ~95-98% then resets, with OOMKilled restarts at 2026-03-21T22:59, 2026-03-22T21:59 and 2026-03-23T19:59; restarts metric increments 0->1->2->3 at exactly those times.

TemplateCache reports unbounded growth with no eviction: 'size=188100 entries, evictions=0' at 18:54 before the OOM, then after restart 'size=9000 entries, evictions=0' at 21:00 and 'size=18000 entries, evictions=0' at 22:00.
CPU is flat ~25% and request_rate is flat ~140 req/s across 2026-03-19 to 2026-03-23, showing no load increase accompanying the memory climb.

consumer_lag for notification-service stays ~50-90 messages normally and spikes only during 2026-03-22T21:00-22:00 (avg 1525, max 17611) and 2026-03-23T19:00-20:00 (avg 1562, max 18137) — i.e. exactly during the OOM/restart windows, not before them.

The only config change was kafka 'log.retention.ms' from 604800000 to 259200000 (Kafka maintenance) at 2026-03-23T18:00:00Z — about 21 hours AFTER the memory climb began at 2026-03-21T01:20 and after two prior OOMs.
kafka CPU is flat ~35% and no kafka WARN/ERROR related to the incident exists; kafka only logged one 'deprecated TLS cipher offered by client' at 17:17:15.
error_rate spikes 5xx (max ~13-14%) occur only in the restart buckets 2026-03-21T20:00, 2026-03-22T20:00, 2026-03-23T16:00 and 2026-03-23T20:00; otherwise error_rate is ~0.2%.
notification-service emits repeated 'heap usage N% over 90 (old gen), full GC took ...ms' WARNs from 2026-03-21T21:37 onward, consistent with a heap filling toward OOM.

refs.quote: heap usage 8% over 90 (old gen), full GC took 4317ms

findings.statement: Dependency graph: notification-service consumes from kafka (queue-consume) and calls external email-provider; kafka is shared and has telemetry, email-provider has none.
Historical incidents HIST-104 and HIST-112 both involve consumer lag spikes after Kafka broker maintenance/reassignment on notification-service/kafka.
